title: Candidate eval scratchpad — Evelyn Torres
content:
Quick context:
- Interview loop: 60m phone screen (me), 90m onsite (system design + coding + culture) with eng-serving-runtime panel.
- Role: Senior/Staff Inference Engineer (focus: runtime perf + kernel/quantization sense).
- Candidate: Evelyn Torres — ex-inference at SignalScale, spent last 3 years on inference perf & kernel tuning for transformer variants.

High-level notes (raw, unedited):
- Comfortable talking low-level (CUDA ideas, memory layout). Gave concrete example of reducing KV-cache copy overhead via fused memcpy + prefetch; explained latency win and memory tradeoffs.
- Strong intuition for batching across heterogeneous request lengths; mentioned dynamic batch shaping and early-exit heuristics.
- Quantization experience: led int8/4 eval, aware of kl-per-channel vs minmax, noted accuracy caveats with attention softmax. Could articulate when to prefer per-channel.
- System design: proposed multi-queue architecture (latency-priority lanes + bulk lanes) with a centralized router that assigns by SLO. Mentioned fallback to cheaper model variants — aligns with Redwood smart routing concept.
- Language: clear, focused on tradeoffs, used numbers when possible (latency drop ~18% for fused path in their anecdote).

Coding / practical:
- Live coding: implemented simplified KV-cache indexing function. Used clean reasoning; missed an edge-case wrap-around until prompted. Fix was small.
- Thought process was good; wrote tests mentally, suggested property-based tests for cache invariants.

Behavioral / partnership: 
- Good at cross-team communication. Described collaborating with infra team to add a kernel-level flag gated by feature flags; emphasized small incremental rollout + perf regression metrics.
- Mentoring: ran brown-bag sessions previously, asked about ramp plan for mentees.

Questions / follow-ups I want answers to:
- Concrete perf numbers on their biggest win (we heard ~18% but need baseline/seq-len details). Ask for the postmortem or PR.
- Any public notes or slides? (They mentioned an internal talk).
- Which quant training pipeline did they use? Looks custom — would like example config.

Red flags:
- Slightly tool-locked (heavy reliance on their internal infra) — but they described migration path and translation to open frameworks.
- One vague answer about multi-tenant security isolation (didn't dive into threats or audit trails). Worth probing with security on follow-up.

Scorecard (1-5, quick):
- Technical depth (kernel / perf): 4
- System design (scalability & routing): 4
- Productionization / ops: 3
- Machine learning fundamentals: 3
- Communication / collaboration: 5
- Overall fit for Senior: strong
- Staff stretch: plausible but would want to see a deeper systems ownership example (end-to-end rollout owning infra + billing impacts).

Suggested next steps: 
- Ask for write-up or PR with the fused memcpy example (linked artifact). If they can share a sanitized artifact, that would bump kernel score to 5.
- Technical take-home: small design/coding exercise on batching strategy under mixed seq lengths (2-3 hours).
- Reference: engineering manager at SignalScale (named), and a peer who worked on quant pipeline.

Panel notes / tweaks to loop: 
- SRE/security quick call to probe multi-tenant isolation thinking (15-20m).
- Swap one behavioral interviewer for someone from optimize (to vet cost-aware tradeoffs).

Action items (me):
- Ping Evelyn for artifacts + availability for take-home (ACTIONS: send template + deadline).
- Add Ayesha to follow-up thread for kernel deep dive.
- Draft brief summary for hiring committee (one paragraph) and include scorecard.

One-paragraph summary (for hiring committee):
Evelyn is a solid inference engineer with demonstrable low-level performance wins and an excellent communicator. She has relevant quantization and KV-cache experience and proposed system designs that align well with Redwood's routing and fallback patterns. Recommend moving to a short take-home and a focused risk call with security; potential hire at Senior now, Staff plausible pending artifacts demonstrating end-to-end ownership and multi-tenant security considerations.

Notes-to-self (loose):
- If artifacts show <10% perf win at real-world seq lengths -> deprioritize kernel claim.
- If artifacts are good, consider leveling for Staff but require leadership examples (roadmap, cross-team shipping).

References / links I should add to final candidate record:
- Linear: INF-4234 (loop + feedback)
- GitHub PR mentioned: runtime/pull/789
- Slack thread: #hiring-inference (search for thread by candidate name)

End of scratchpad.
